profile.entities: JK Tyre & Industries Ltd (Parent); JK Tornel (Mexico Subsidiary)
profile.subseg: Truck Bus Radial (TBR); Passenger Car Radial (PCR); Farm Tyres; 2/3 Wheeler Tyres; Mexico Operations (JK Tornel)
profile.themes: West Asia Crisis Input Cost Shock; Aggressive Brownfield Capacity Expansion; Premiumization & Product Mix Shift; AI-Driven Manufacturing Efficiency

bull_bear.body: Debt utilized for expansion (Net Debt up Rs 364 Cr to Rs 4,445 Cr); Working capital borrowings reduced significantly (Rs 2,378 Cr to Rs 1,808 Cr); Cash balance decreased to Rs 301 Cr from Rs 711 Cr as QIP funds deployed into capex; Focus on maintaining comfortable leverage ratios (Net Debt/EBITDA 2.13x).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical instability (West Asia) causing raw material volatility and supply chain disruptions; Potential demand moderation in H2FY27 if price hikes are not fully passed through; Trade uncertainty in Mexico (US tariffs, USMCA review); Intense competition from new entrants in TBR/PCR segments.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and aggressive on growth (record volumes, massive capex commitment) but cautious on near-term margins due to external macro shocks; Emphasizes operational discipline, premiumization, and digital transformation (AI) as key moats.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly highlighted 'Agentic AI' deployment for decision-making and workflow automation, moving beyond basic analytics; The 'Selling Miles' fleet management program is positioned as a significant entry barrier against new competitors by creating service-based stickiness rather than just product sales; Mexico subsidiary (JK Tornel) facing sluggishness due to US tariff uncertainty despite stable full-year revenue.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body: - The deck does not provide explicit details on dividend policy, balance sheet strategy, or reinvestment philosophy beyond financial performance metrics.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: TBR: Replacement +19%, OE +53% YoY; PCR: Replacement +10%, OE +26% YoY (Premium 16'+ grew 13%); Farm: +58% YoY (OE nearly doubled); 2/3W: OE +72%, Replacement +39% QoQ. Market Mix Q4: 63% Replacement, 27% OE, 10% Export. Category Mix: TBR 56%, PCR 27%, Non-Truck Bias 13%, 2/3W 4%.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Surge in raw material costs (18-20%) pressuring margins for players unable to pass on prices quickly. | JK Tyre & Industries Ltd | beneficiary | High | Already implemented 4-7% price hikes and has strong premium mix to absorb shock; full capacity utilization allows immediate monetization of any demand. |
| Capacity constraints limiting growth for competitors without immediate expansion plans. | JK Tyre & Industries Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Massive Rs 6,110 Cr capex plan positions them to capture market share as demand grows, though execution risk exists. |
| US tariff uncertainty and trade tensions affecting Mexican manufacturing exports. | JK Tornel (Subsidiary) | loser | Med | Q4 sluggishness attributed to geopolitical volatility; reliance on USMCA renewal creates near-term overhang. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Pioneers of radial technology in India with multiple firsts: first OE fitment of tubeless passenger radials, first to launch H/V/Z-rated passenger radials, and first to introduce Truck/Bus Radial Tyres.
- Globally ranked 19th top tyre company, with presence in 100+ countries and a strong domestic network of 6,000+ dealers and 900+ exclusive brand shops.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Brand Recognition] Conferred 'SUPER BRANDS 2025' and recognised as 'ET ICONIC BRANDS OF INDIA 2025'.
- [R&D Capability] Asia's first and India's foremost R&D Centre with 200+ scientists, 7 patents granted, and India's biggest Anechoic Chamber for noise and vibration analysis.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Revenue: Rs 4,233 Cr (Q4, +12% YoY), Rs 16,384 Cr (FY26, +11% YoY); EBITDA: Rs 546 Cr (Q4, +42% YoY), Margin 12.9% (+270 bps YoY); PAT: Rs 188 Cr (Q4, +83% YoY), Rs 774 Cr (FY26, +50% YoY); Order Book: No specific volume order book disclosed, but management confirms no OEM order cuts and full capacity utilization (>90%); Net Debt: Rs 4,445 Cr (up Rs 364 Cr YoY due to expansion loans), Net Debt/EBITDA improved to 2.13x. One-offs: Other income declined sequentially as QIP funds (Rs 700+ Cr) were deployed from fixed deposits into capex projects.
latest_quarter.title: Financial scorecard

latest_quarter.body: Q4 RM basket +1.3% QoQ, flat YoY; Q1FY27 RM costs projected to surge 18-20% due to West Asia crisis and rupee weakness. Mitigation: 4-5% price hike in domestic replacement, 5-7% in exports already implemented; additional 5-6% hike underway. OEM price increases will lag. Management expects crude softening post-Q2 to ease pressure.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Mid-single digit expected for FY27 auto industry; Margins: Under pressure in Q1FY27 due to 18-20% RM cost hike, mitigated by 4-7% price hikes already taken and further 5-6% planned; Order Inflow: Buoyant demand expected, no OEM cancellations; Capex: Rs 1,200 Cr outlay for FY27, part of Rs 6,110 Cr total expansion (Rs 1,130 Cr ongoing + Rs 4,980 Cr new) to complete by FY29.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: No explicit numerical order book provided; qualitative indicators show full capacity utilization (>90%) across segments, robust OEM approvals (Tata, Ashok Leyland, Mahindra, etc.), and no order cancellations despite geopolitical uncertainty.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Rs 4,980 Cr new brownfield expansion approved to increase TBR & PCR capacity by 24% by FY29; Premiumization strategy (Shresth Plus, Levitas Ultra) driving higher realizations; 'Selling Miles' fleet management program creating sticky B2B relationships; Outsourcing strategy to rapidly scale 2/3W segment without heavy asset investment.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: JK Tyre delivered record FY26 profitability with 270 bps margin expansion in Q4 driven by volume growth and mix, but faces immediate Q1FY27 headwinds from an 18-20% raw material cost surge due to geopolitical tensions. Management is countering this with staggered price hikes and committing to a massive Rs 6,110 crore capex plan through FY29 to alleviate >90% capacity utilization, signaling strong confidence in long-term structural demand despite short-term inflationary noise.

open.item: Rs.1,400 crore projects to start from Q3FY26 with ramp-up over next 6 months; FY26 capex outlay Rs.900-1,000 crore.
CIL-JK Tyre amalgamation approved by SEBI, now with NCLT and progressing well.
JK Tornel PCR expansion project of USD 27 million progressing, expected to be completed by end of CY2025.
Cavendish-JK Tyre amalgamation progressing (approval processes ongoing).
Board approved amalgamation of Cavendish (CIL) into JK Tyre at swap ratio of 92 JK Tyre shares per 100 CIL shares; expected to complete within 10-12 months.
Management targets mid-double-digit consolidated revenue growth going forward, in line with Q3's 15% YoY.
Q4FY26 RM basket expected to remain rangebound, inching up 1-2%; margins to stay intact via volume and premiumization.
Q4FY26 expected to be very strong with healthy growth across sectors, momentum expected to continue into FY27 on GST, rural demand and lower rates.
Cavendish revenue expected to recover to Rs.1,000-1,100 crore quarterly average with margins returning to JK Tyre standalone levels.
Tornel exports to US (~7-8% of Mexico sales) expected to rise under USMCA/tariff postponement; new ATV tyre business initiated for US market.
Management expects to return to its guided EBITDA margin range as RM stays rangebound and margin-accretive PCR/TBR/ASLTR projects ramp.
Plan to raise PCR 16-inch-and-above premium mix from current 26% to around 40% in coming quarters.
Full-year FY26 guided to initial double-digit growth, better than FY25, led by replacement.
JK Tornel FY26 performance and margins expected to be better than FY25, aided by zero US tariff on Mexican tyres and better mix.
Rs.1,400 crore PCR/TBR/ASLTR projects to yield available capacities within FY26; ~Rs.900 crore capex outlay planned for FY26.
Full-year FY25 RM up ~10%, selling price ~7% passed on; ~3% under-recovery remains to be recouped.
Management guides to high-single-digit to double-digit consolidated revenue growth in FY26, led by replacement and new capacities.
Longer-term EBITDA margin range guided at 12-15%; efforts to pass on FY25 under-recovery into FY26 to normalise margins.
TBR and PCR replacement identified as the two key growth segments for FY26; PCR replacement grew 24% YoY and overall replacement 16% YoY in Q3.
Rs.1,400 crore brownfield TBR/PCR/ASLTR projects to be commissioned broadly in H2FY26 with ramp-up over next 2-3 quarters; expected 1.1-1.2x asset turns.
